# GEO report: atlas-roadmaps **New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. ## Code score: 40/100, At risk Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points). How it's calculated: low = 12.58 ÷ 23 × 100 = 55. High = (12.58 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 55. The cap of 40 applies because `robots.txt` blocks Bingbot from the whole site, against your declared policy of allowing AI search. Without the cap the score would be 55. Almost every rule was settled from the code. The score is held down by one robots.txt block and a few small gaps. ## Live check - **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL. ## Do these first ### 1. Stop blocking Bingbot - **Why it matters:** Bing's crawler is told to skip every page, and your config says search crawlers should be allowed. It also makes every page non-indexable for Bing (GEO-009 and GEO-014). - **Where:** `public/robots.txt:5-6` - **What the code says:** `User-agent: Bingbot` / `Disallow: /` - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** 81 (the cap is lifted) ### 2. Point robots.txt at the sitemap - **Why it matters:** Crawlers have no declared way to find `sitemap.xml`. - **Where:** `public/robots.txt` (no `Sitemap:` line anywhere in the file) - **What the code says:** the file ends at `Disallow: /` on line 9. - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** 89 (with item 1) ### 3. Load the changelog on the server - **Why it matters:** The entries are fetched in the browser, so the server HTML has an empty list (GEO-003). - **Where:** `app/routes/changelog.tsx:5` - **What the code says:** `useEffect(() => { fetch('/api/changelog')...` - **Size:** Medium - **Score after this:** 93 (with items 1 and 2) ## All results | Rule | What it checks | Code | Where | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | GEO-013 | robots.txt valid | Clear | `public/robots.txt` is valid | | GEO-009 | Search crawlers allowed | Problem | `robots.txt:5-6` Bingbot blocked site-wide | | GEO-014 | Routes indexable | Problem | Bingbot block hits all 4 routes | | GEO-015 | Absolute canonical | Problem | `pricing.tsx` has none (3 of 4 routes clear) | | GEO-003 | Content in server HTML | Problem | `changelog.tsx:5` (3 of 4 routes clear) | | GEO-004 | JSON-LD valid | Not applicable | No JSON-LD found | | GEO-011 | Sitemap discoverable | Problem | No `Sitemap:` line in robots.txt | | GEO-012 | Title, description, lang | Problem | `pricing.tsx` has no meta, so it inherits the generic `root.tsx:2` title "Atlas" (3 of 4 routes clear) | | GEO-016 | Server-rendered links | Problem | `_index.tsx:9` is the only path to `/features` (2 of 3 routes clear) | | GEO-017 | Snippet restrictions | Clear | No nosnippet or header config | | GEO-002 | Accessibility basics | Clear | Read `root.tsx` and the 5 routes. No images, and the links have text | | GEO-101 | App association files | Not applicable | No mobile app declared | | GEO-010 | llms.txt (info only) | Not applicable | Not present, not scored | | GEO-102 | App structured data (info only) | Not applicable | Not scored | ## Other problems found - `app/routes/_index.tsx:9`: `
navigate('/features')}>`. This is a clickable div, not a link. Use ``. It's also why `/features` is not in the navigation (`root.tsx:7`). - `robots.txt:2-3`: `/dashboard` is disallowed and also `noindex` (`dashboard.tsx:1`). Crawlers can't fetch the page to see the noindex, so keep one of the two. This looks deliberate, so it isn't scored. ## Worth considering - **Give pricing its own head:** `app/routes/pricing.tsx:1`: `

Pricing

`. It has no `meta` export, so it uses "Atlas". Add a title, description and canonical. - **Back up the integrations claim:** `_index.tsx:8`: `Integrates with all the tools you already use.` Nothing names a tool. List the real integrations. - **Pricing says nothing concrete:** `pricing.tsx:1`: `Talk to us for a quote.` Add plan names and what each includes, if you can share them. - **Add `` to the sitemap:** `public/sitemap.xml:3-6`. The changelog has real release dates to use. - **Add Organization/WebSite structured data:** `root.tsx` has no JSON-LD. Add one with the name "Atlas" and the origin from `geo.config.json`. - **Add `charset` and `viewport`:** `root.tsx:6` only renders `` and ``. - **Link onward:** `features.tsx:2` and `pricing.tsx:1` have no links to each other or to the changelog. Cross-link them. - **Give changelog entries their own pages:** `changelog.tsx:6` renders each release as a bare `
  • `. Separate addresses would let each release be found and cited. - **Make the site name consistent:** the home title says "Atlas: roadmaps for product teams" and the others say "| Atlas". Pick one pattern. - **Use a clear name in `root.tsx:2`:** the default title "Atlas" alone doesn't say what the site is. ## Can't tell from code - **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs ` to check real crawlers against their published addresses. - **Real responses:** status codes and redirects need a live check. `/api/changelog` has no route in this repo, so it may fail. ## Assumptions - You want AI search tools to find this site. `geo.config.json` says `aiSearchCrawlers: allow`. - Blocking GPTBot (`robots.txt:8-9`) matches `trainingCrawlers: block`, so it isn't counted. - `/dashboard` is private on purpose. ## What to do next 1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written. 2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more. 3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL. Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
